headline: High: Roo Code’s filesystem/MCP/write capabilities can collide with kotaemon’s broad egress and file-backed workspace, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP, while kotaemon processes documents, HTML, MHTML, and chat transcripts in ./ktem_app_data. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if kotaemon outputs are copied into Roo Code or shared through files. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs are placed into a shared workspace file that Roo Code opens
IF an MCP server forwards kotaemon-generated content into Roo Code without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep kotaemon and Roo Code in separate directories
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted text
Use a read-only handoff file for any copied outputs
Add a manual review step before pasting content into Roo Code

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and broad document classes, and Roo Code has broad filesystem read/write plus broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files, Roo Code can read sensitive artifacts and transmit them through configured model APIs or MCP. The pairwise leakage path is therefore dangerous in default developer setups.
conditions: IF kotaemon stores API keys or sensitive documents in a directory readable by Roo Code
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace contents to a remote model or MCP server
mitigations: Move secrets out of any shared workspace
Restrict Roo Code to a separate project folder
Turn off remote model providers for sensitive sessions
Use OS permissions to block cross-tool file reads
Rotate any exposed API keys

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; kotaemon also supports multiple instances and uses a file-backed app data directory. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git mutations can overwrite each other. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the conflict is materially unsafe.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem tree
IF Roo Code performs git commits or file writes while kotaemon is also active
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces to each agent
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git branches per agent
Enable filesystem snapshots or backups
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and perform tool actions, while kotaemon produces document-centric outputs and citations. If Roo Code treats kotaemon output as authoritative, a mistaken extraction can cascade into edits, commits, or external actions. No verification workflow is documented between them, so the default risk is high.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes kotaemon-generated summaries or citations without independent verification
IF Roo Code uses those outputs to edit files, commit code, or trigger shell actions
mitigations: Require human review before any action based on kotaemon output
Cross-check key facts against source documents
Disable auto-commit or auto-run workflows
Limit Roo Code to draft-only mode for shared tasks

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and chat transcripts, while Roo Code handles model-provider API keys and workspace files. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into a shared workspace, differing retention and residency controls can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not document a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF sensitive chat transcripts or API keys are stored in a workspace shared by both agents
IF one agent’s configured model provider retains data longer than the other agent’s local storage policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Review provider retention settings before use
Document which agent may store which data class
Delete temporary files after each session
